name: GitHub Codespaces

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go machine types (per active hour)
modes.note: Official price table: $0.18/$0.36/$0.72/$1.44/$2.88 per hour for 2/4/8/16/32-core = $0.09 per core-hour, same price in every region. Compute billed for the whole time the codespace is 'active' (created/started until stopped, deleted or idle-timed-out), regardless of CPU use; usage reported to billing hourly, billed monthly; exact rounding unpublished. RAM is 4 GB/core (official for 2-core 8 GB and 32-core 128 GB; intermediate RAM follows the same ratio). Disk: 2-core 32 GB and 32-core 128 GB official; 4-core 32 GB and 8-core 64 GB from a GitHub community thread (a 4-core/64 GB variant also exists); 16-core disk not published. No 4-core/8 GB shape: a 4 vCPU / 8 GiB workload lands on the 4-core/16 GB machine. Availability of larger machines may be limited by org policy or repo minimum spec.

plans.name: Personal account: GitHub Free
plans.note: Per personal account per month: 120 core-hours (= 60 h on 2-core, 30 h on 4-core; $10.80 at list) + 15 GB-month storage ($1.05, separate quota, not in included_usd). Quota applies only to codespaces billed to that user. Without a payment method usage is BLOCKED once either quota runs out; with one, overage billed at list, subject to the user's budgets.

plans.name: Personal account: GitHub Pro
plans.note: 180 core-hours ($16.20 at list) + 20 GB-month ($1.40) per month. The GitHub Pro subscription price is not stated on the live docs or github.com/pricing (the widely cited $4/month is from prior research / third parties), so fee is null.

plans.name: Organization: GitHub Team (org-owned codespaces)
plans.note: No free Codespaces quota for orgs. $4/user/month (github.com/pricing shows '$4 USD per user/month for the first 12 months *'; post-12-month price not shown). Org pays only if codespaces are set to organization-owned, the user is enabled, and the org has no Codespaces budget or a non-zero one; pricing page lists Team as 'Ability to increase spend limit'. Orgs on GitHub Free cannot pay for Codespaces ('$0 spend limit'), so users pay personally.

plans.name: Organization: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
plans.note: 'Starting at $21 USD per user/month for the first 12 months *'. Same Codespaces list rates; adds SAML SSO, enterprise/cost-center budgets, audit logs, data residency. Volume discounts via sales unpublished. Codespaces not available for repos owned by Enterprise Managed User accounts (only org-billed).

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: How sessions end (idle timeout tail is billed)

options.label: Stopped explicitly at end of work (no tail)
Left to default 30-min idle timeout (8 h session +6.25%)

knobs.why: Compute is billed while a codespace is active, used or not; it only stops when stopped/deleted or after the idle timeout (default 30 min, 5-240 min). Factors assume an 8-hour session; scale mentally for other lengths. Terminal output (e.g. a served app logging requests) resets the idle timer.

caveats: Compute price per machine type is official ($0.09/core-hour); 'included usage multiplier' = core count, so free quotas are core-hours, not wall-clock hours (120 core-hours = 30 h on a 4-core).
Billing granularity/rounding is not published (usage 'reported to the billing service every hour'); granularity_s null.

Storage is $0.07/GB-month metered in GB-hours of USED space (repo, data, extensions, custom dev-container image), not the machine's disk size. Default universal image is free. Billed while the codespace exists, running or stopped; accumulated storage for the month is not reduced by deleting.

Stopped codespaces auto-delete after the retention period (default and max 30 days; 0 = delete on stop), except 'Keep codespace' which retains indefinitely (storage billed). Org policy can cap retention. snapshot_gib_month = stopped-codespace storage rate; no memory state is kept. features.snapshot = 'fs' (verifier 2026-09-28, was 'none', which made the engine reject retained-state workloads): no snapshot API, but a stopped codespace keeps its filesystem.

Prebuilds: built with GitHub Actions minutes (billed as Actions) plus storage at $0.07/GB-month per prebuild per region per retained version (default all regions x 2 versions). Not modelled in the card.

Org billing is gated by budgets: the org pays only if it has no Codespaces budget or a non-zero one; 'Stop usage when budget limit is reached' blocks create/resume. The '$0 default spending limit' for orgs is legacy wording; the current pricing page shows Free orgs with a '$0 spend limit' and Team/Enterprise with 'Ability to increase spend limit'.

Team $4 and Enterprise $21 per user/month are shown as 'for the first 12 months *' on github.com/pricing; the footnoted later price was not captured. Seat fees are for GitHub itself, not Codespaces-specific.
Egress set to 0: the billing doc says a codespace incurs two charges (compute and storage); no network charge is documented anywhere.
Regions from the REST API geo enum (UsEast, UsWest, EuropeWest, SoutheastAsia); older research also listed Australia, not found in current docs. No regional price difference.
RAM per machine = 4 GB/core (official at 2- and 32-core). 4-core/8-core disk sizes from a GitHub community thread (third-party-grade); 16-core disk unpublished. No GPU machine types in current docs.

Personal free quota is carried as plan included_usd (compute only), not free.monthly_credit, to avoid double counting; it is per personal account, so a team of N developers each billing their own account gets N quotas (engine sees one).
No benchmark data in this research set (perf all null). Cold create without prebuild takes tens of seconds to minutes (unmeasured).

Per-user caps exist but are unpublished: docs (Creating a codespace for a repository, 2026-09-28) say "There are limits to the number of codespaces you can create, and the number of codespaces you can run at the same time. These limits vary based on a number of factors." A fleet of dozens of concurrent codespaces on one personal account is unlikely to be allowed; org-owned codespaces spread over many users are the realistic route. Numbers unknown, so plan.concurrency stays null.

Idle timeout: default 30 min, configurable 5-240 min (4 h). Activity = typing/mouse or terminal input or output; a background process with no terminal output does not count, so an unattended agent that prints nothing stops after at most 4 h idle. No hard session cap otherwise (not encoded as max_session_h because a loop that writes to a terminal stays active).
GPU machine type was deprecated by 2025-08-29 (NCv3 retirement); features.gpu=false is correct and should cite this.

Org policy 'Maximum codespaces per user' can cap org-billed codespaces per user (active + stopped); separately 'The number of organization-billed codespaces someone can create is governed by a limit to the total number of codespaces that they can create across all repositories they can access. This limit is set by GitHub.' (value unpublished).
Prebuild storage is a separate billing SKU (codespaces_prebuild_storage) from codespaces_storage; both at the $0.07/GB-month storage rate and both count toward the Codespaces budget.
